text: When you let go of what you are, you become what you might be.
author: Lao Tzu

text: Three things cannot be long hidden: the sun, the moon, and the truth.
author: Buddha

text: In the end, only three things matter: how much you loved, how gently you lived, and how gracefully you let go of things not meant for you.
author: Buddha

text: Peace comes from within. Do not seek it without.
author: Buddha

text: Every morning we are born again. What we do today is what matters most.
author: Buddha

text: Mind is everything. What you think you become.
author: Buddha

author: Buddha

text: Hatred does not cease by hatred, but only by love; this is the eternal rule.
author: Buddha

text: There is no fire like passion, no shark like hatred, no snare like folly, no torrent like greed and lust.

text: The mind acts as a mirror: what you put in is what comes back to you.
author: Buddha

text: Easeful death is but a phase of transition and not a finale.
author: Buddha

text: The one who has renounced violence towards all living beings, weak or strong, who neither kills nor causes others to kill — him I call a brahmin.
author: Buddha

text: To conquer oneself is a mightier victory than to conquer all other men.
author: Buddha

text: Life is a bridge; cross over it but do not build a house on it.
author: Buddha

text: A monk who has attained the unconditioned does not cling to life, does not cling to death, but waits with equanimity.
author: Buddha

text: When the mind is free, there is no more suffering. This is the truth.
author: Buddha

text: I teach one thing: suffering and the end of suffering.
author: Buddha

text: The middle way is the path that avoids extremes and leads to wisdom and clarity.

text: What is not eternal is not worth clinging to. Release and you will find freedom.
author: Buddha

text: Impermanence is not a cause for grief; it is a teacher. Listen to it and you will understand the nature of existence.

text: Goodness comes to those who practice it. Evil comes to those who plant it.
author: Buddha

text: When you sit in meditation, do not fight your thoughts. Simply notice them as clouds passing through the sky.

text: The ego is the greatest obstacle to awakening. When you see through it, liberation is near.

text: The eightfold path — right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration — is the road to the end of suffering.

author: Buddha

text: The root of all suffering is attachment. Let go, and you will find peace.
author: Buddha

text: Karma is not fate. It is the sum of your choices, and it can be transformed by wisdom and right action.
author: Buddha

text: The present moment is the only moment available to us, and it is the doorway to all moments.

text: Mindfulness is the miracle by which we master and restore ourselves.

text: When we are truly aware, we see the interconnectedness of all living things.

text: Smile, breathe, and go slowly. This is the way to happiness.

text: We have more possibilities in each moment than we can imagine.
